title: Whack-a-Mole 3D
prompt:
Create a complete HTML file with a 3D Whack-a-Mole game using Three.js and GLTFLoader.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 8, 10) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0 and castShadow enabled.
- The ground is a large green plane (20x20) at y=0 with receiveShadow.
- Create a 3x3 grid of "mole holes" — brown cylinders (radius 0.6, height 0.15) placed at positions: row/col from -2 to 2 with spacing 2.5 (i.e., x and z values: -2.5, 0, 2.5). Each hole is at y=0.075.
- Load the 3D model 'BrainStem.glb' using GLTFLoader from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js'. Scale it to (0.4, 0.4, 0.4). Clone this model for each of the 9 holes. Each mole model sits below its hole (y = -1.5) when hidden and animates up to y = 0.5 when popping up. Assign each mole a userData.holeIndex from 0-8 (row-major order).

## Game Mechanics
- The game has three phases: 'waiting', 'playing', 'gameover'.
- A DOM button with id='startButton' reads 'Start Game'. Clicking it starts the game, sets phase to 'playing', resets score to 0, misses to 0, molesWhacked to 0, and starts a 30-second countdown timer.
- During 'playing', every 1.2 seconds a random mole pops up (animates from y=-1.5 to y=0.5 over 0.3s). A mole stays up for 1.5 seconds, then goes back down (animates over 0.3s). Only up to 2 moles can be visible at once.
- The player clicks on a visible (popped-up) mole using raycasting. A successful hit: increment score by 10, immediately animate the mole back down, briefly flash the mole red (0.2s), and increment molesWhacked.
- If a mole goes back down without being clicked, increment misses by 1.
- Each successful whack plays a short visual particle burst: 8 small yellow spheres that fly outward from the mole position and fade over 0.5s.
- When the timer reaches 0, set phase to 'gameover'. Show a DOM overlay div with id='gameOverOverlay' displaying 'Game Over! Score: {score}'.
- A 'combo' system: consecutive hits without a miss multiply score. First hit = 10, second consecutive = 20, third = 30, etc. A miss resets the combo multiplier to 1. Track currentCombo (number of consecutive hits) and maxCombo.

## HUD / UI
- A div with id='hud' at top-left showing: 'Score: {score} | Time: {timeLeft}s | Combo: x{currentCombo}'
- The startButton should be centered on screen, and hidden once the game starts.
- The gameOverOverlay should be hidden until gameover, centered, semi-transparent black background, white text.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- phase: 'waiting' | 'playing' | 'gameover' (string)
- score: number (current score)
- timeLeft: number (seconds remaining, integer)
- molesWhacked: number (total moles successfully hit)
- misses: number (total misses)
- currentCombo: number (current consecutive hit streak, starts at 0)
- maxCombo: number (highest combo achieved)
- activeMoles: number (count of currently visible/popped-up moles, 0-2)
- totalPops: number (total number of times a mole has popped up)
- molePositions: array of 9 objects {x, y, z} representing each mole's current world position
- particlesActive: number (count of active particle bursts currently animating)
- gameStarted: boolean (true once start has been clicked at least once)
- modelLoaded: boolean (true once the GLB model is fully loaded)

## Technical Requirements
- Use requestAnimationFrame loop.
- Use THREE.Raycaster for click detection.
- Smooth animation (lerp or tween) for mole up/down movement.
- Renderer should have shadowMap enabled, antialias true, and fill the window.
- Handle window resize.
- Import Three.js and GLTFLoader from CDN (jsdelivr, version 0.160.0) using ES module imports.
physics_constraints: Moles must animate smoothly between y=-1.5 (hidden) and y=0.5 (visible). Only up to 2 moles can be active simultaneously. Pop-up interval is 1.2s. Mole stays up for 1.5s. Animation duration is 0.3s. Timer counts down from 30. Combo multiplier increments linearly with consecutive hits.
